A atuação da Softex em programas estratégicos, inovação, internacionalização e desenvolvimento de competências digitais contribui para ampliar oportunidades, estimular a competitividade e fortalecer o posicionamento do Brasil na economia digital global. Parcerias como essa são fundamentais para construirmos um ambiente cada vez mais inovador, inclusivo e preparado para os desafios do futuro. Luciana Santos Ministra do MCTI MCTI A inserção competitiva do Brasil na economia digital global passa, necessariamente, pela capacidade de conectar inovação, tecnologia e internacionalização. Nesse contexto, a atuação da Softex tem sido estratégica para fortalecer empresas brasileiras de tecnologia, ampliar oportunidades de negócios e posicionar o país de forma mais relevante no cenário internacional. A parceria entre a ApexBrasil e a Softex demonstra como a cooperação entre instituições pode impulsionar exportações, estimular inovação e abrir caminhos para que empresas brasileiras ampliem sua presença em mercados globais. Iniciativas voltadas à internacionalização do setor de TIC contribuem não apenas para o crescimento econômico, mas também para o fortalecimento da imagem do Brasil como referência em tecnologia e transformação digital. Laudemir Müller Presidente da ApexBrasil ApexBrasil A crescente adoção da Inteligência Artificial nos negócios exige visão de longo prazo, desenvolvimento de talentos e colaboração entre diferentes atores do ecossistema tecnológico. Nesse contexto, a Softex vem desempenhando um papel relevante ao conectar empresas, governo, academia e iniciativas estratégicas voltadas ao fortalecimento da tecnologia brasileira. O Brasil tem a oportunidade de assumir uma posição de destaque nessa nova fase de transformação impulsionada pela IA. Para isso, é fundamental estimular a formação de profissionais qualificados, apoiar o empreendedorismo e criar condições para que a tecnologia seja aplicada na resolução de desafios reais de negócios e da sociedade. A atuação da Softex contribui para fortalecer essa agenda, ampliando a capacidade de inovação, a competitividade das empresas e o desenvolvimento tecnológico do país. Marco Stefanini Founder & CEO Global Stefanini Gostaria de destacar e agradecer a parceria entre a Softex e o Instituto Federal do Ceará (IFCE), que se estende também à Rede Federal de Educação Profissional, Científica e Tecnológica. Essa atuação conjunta tem alavancado de forma significativa as questões relacionadas à formação de capital humano e intelectual, além das estratégias voltadas para o mundo digital. Esse trabalho tem permitido que o Brasil avance e conquiste espaços cada vez mais estratégicos do ponto de vista da inovação, da pesquisa aplicada e da conexão com o mercado, um setor que demanda inovação todos os dias e em alta velocidade. É justamente nessa perspectiva de velocidade, formação e entregas reais que a parceria entre a Softex e o IFCE vem contribuindo para impulsionar a indústria, o comércio, a tecnologia, a inovação e todo esse universo criativo e transformador. A Softex tem sido esse braço de execução, realização e entrega, ajudando a transformar conhecimento em resultados concretos para a sociedade e para o desenvolvimento do país. Essa atuação colaborativa é fundamental para ampliar a competitividade brasileira e preparar o país para os desafios e oportunidades da nova economia digital. A Softex desempenha um papel relevante ao impulsionar iniciativas voltadas à inovação, capacitação e expansão internacional do setor de TIC, aproximando empresas, talentos e parceiros estratégicos. Essa colaboração fortalece a presença do Brasil na economia digital global e demonstra o potencial da tecnologia brasileira como vetor de desenvolvimento, competitividade e transformação econômica. Nesse contexto, a parceria com a Softex fortalece nossa missão de conectar inovação, conhecimento e desenvolvimento humano, contribuindo para a formação de protagonistas capazes de gerar impacto positivo no ecossistema brasileiro de tecnologia e inovação. Ao unir expertise, inovação e alcance nacional, essa colaboração amplia oportunidades de capacitação, estimula a inclusão de novos profissionais no mercado e contribui para a formação de mão de obra qualificada em áreas estratégicas como inteligência artificial e semicondutores. Mais do que desenvolver competências técnicas, a parceria ajuda a conectar educação, inovação e setor produtivo, gerando impactos positivos para empresas, instituições e para a competitividade do Brasil no cenário tecnológico global. titulo: Estrutura organizacional e governança da Softex
descricao_resumida: MAPA DO SITE Estrutura organizacional ASSEMBLEIA GERAL CONSELHO ADMINISTRATIVO
descricao_completa: MAPA DO SITE Estrutura organizacional ASSEMBLEIA GERAL CONSELHO ADMINISTRATIVO CONSELHO FISCAL Estabelece as diretrizes gerais da Softex e reúne-se periodicamente para deliberar sobre temas estratégicos, garantindo a conformidade das iniciativas com os objetivos institucionais. Delibera e orienta estrategicamente a entidade. É composto por representantes do poder público, entidades da sociedade civil e membros eleitos pela Assembleia e pelo próprio Conselho. Compete a ele eleger e destituir a Diretoria Executiva, aprovar orçamento e investimentos, fiscalizar metas e validar demonstrativos financeiros e contábeis após auditoria externa credenciada pela CVM e análise do Conselho Fiscal. Supervisiona as finanças e operações da Softex, garantindo o uso ético, eficiente e transparente dos recursos. Examina contas, demonstrações financeiras e relatórios da entidade, emitindo pareceres encaminhados ao Conselho de Administração. Diretoria Executiva Presidente da Softex Christian Tadeu Christian Tadeu é presidente da Softex e empresário do setor de Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicação (TIC), com ampla experiência em gestão empresarial, inovação e desenvolvimento do ecossistema digital brasileiro. Formado em Administração de Empresas e Contabilidade, atua há quase três décadas no fortalecimento da competitividade, do empreendedorismo e da transformação digital no país. Com trajetória consolidada em entidades representativas e institucionais, presidiu organizações como a Assespro/DF e integrou instâncias estratégicas ligadas à inovação e tecnologia, como a Câmara de Inovação e Tecnologia da Fecomércio/DF e o Conselho Nacional do Comércio (CNC). À frente da Softex, lidera iniciativas voltadas à promoção da inovação, ao desenvolvimento da indústria nacional de software e à ampliação de oportunidades por meio da tecnologia, contribuindo para o posicionamento do Brasil como protagonista na economia digital. Vice-presidente da Softex Diônes Lima Diônes Lima é vice-presidente da Softex, especialista em inovação e gestão de projetos pela Escola de Negócios de Barcelona, com formação executiva em gestão de negócios pela Fundação Dom Cabral (FDC) e mestrado em Business Administration Global pela Universidade Isabel I de Castela. Com ampla experiência na formulação e execução de políticas, programas e iniciativas voltadas ao desenvolvimento da inovação e do empreendedorismo no Brasil, atuou na estruturação e implementação de projetos estratégicos nas áreas de tecnologia, transformação digital e fortalecimento do ecossistema de inovação. Na Softex, contribui para a articulação de iniciativas nacionais voltadas ao desenvolvimento tecnológico, à capacitação, ao empreendedorismo inovador e à promoção de políticas públicas para o setor de TIC, com foco na geração de impacto e no fortalecimento da economia digital brasileira. Compliance Softex O Programa de Governança, Compliance e Proteção de Dados da Softex está alinhado às melhores práticas de integridade, segurança e transparência. Mais do que diretrizes, sustenta a atuação da instituição na execução de políticas públicas e no desenvolvimento do ecossistema digital, garantindo confiabilidade em suas iniciativas. A Softex reforça seu compromisso com a ética, a privacidade e a transparência, promovendo um ambiente seguro e responsável para a sociedade. descricao_completa: Oczekiwany wynik: Oczekuje się, że wyniki projektu przyczynią się do osiągnięcia następujących rezultatów: Dla wspieranych doktorantów nowe badania naukowe oraz zbywalne umiejętności i kompetencje, prowadzące do zwiększenia szans na zatrudnienie i perspektyw zawodowych w środowisku akademickim i poza nim; nowa wiedza umożliwiająca przekształcanie pomysłów w produkty i usługi, w stosownych przypadkach; Zwiększone zdolności w zakresie tworzenia sieci kontaktów i komunikacji z partnerami naukowymi, a także z ogółem społeczeństwa, które zwiększą i poszerzą wpływ badań naukowych i innowacji. Dla organizacji uczestniczących poprawa jakości, adekwatności i trwałości programów studiów doktoranckich i rozwiązań w zakresie nadzoru; Wzmocniona współpraca i transfer wiedzy między sektorami i dyscyplinami; większa integracja działań szkoleniowych i badawczych między organizacjami uczestniczącymi; Zwiększona zdolność w zakresie badań naukowych i innowacji; zwiększenie umiędzynarodowienia i atrakcyjności; Regularne przekazywanie informacji zwrotnych na temat wyników badań w zakresie nauczania i edukacji w organizacjach uczestniczących. Zakres stosowania: Sieci doktoranckie MSCA będą wdrażać programy doktoranckie poprzez partnerstwa uniwersytetów, instytucji badawczych i infrastruktur badawczych, przedsiębiorstw, w tym MŚP, oraz innych podmiotów społeczno-gospodarczych z różnych krajów w całej Europie i poza nią. Sieci doktoranckie MSCA są rzeczywiście otwarte na udział organizacji z państw trzecich w celu wspierania strategicznych partnerstw międzynarodowych na rzecz szkolenia i wymiany naukowców. Te programy doktoranckie będą odpowiadać dobrze określonym potrzebom w różnych obszarach badań i innowacji, narażać naukowców na sektor akademicki i pozaakademicki oraz oferować szkolenia w zakresie badań naukowych, a także zbywalne umiejętności i kompetencje istotne dla innowacji i długoterminowych szans na zatrudnienie (np. przedsiębiorczość, komercjalizacja wyników, prawa własności intelektualnej, komunikacja). Propozycje dotyczące sieci doktorskich mogą odzwierciedlać istniejące lub planowane partnerstwa badawcze między organizacjami uczestniczącymi. Procedura naboru doktorantów musi być otwarta, przejrzysta i oparta na osiągnięciach, zgodnie z Europejską kartą naukowca. Ogłoszenie o naborze (które ma być szeroko ogłaszane na całym świecie, w tym na stronie internetowej EURAXESS [1]) musi zawierać informację, czy publikowane stawki obejmują wszystkie podatki i składki pracodawcy i pracownika. W miarę możliwości należy opublikować wynagrodzenie brutto (wynagrodzenie netto + podatki i składki pracownika). Sieci doktoranckie MSCA zachęca się do prowadzenia doktoratów przemysłowych lub wspólnych. doktoraty przemysłowe Dzięki doktoratom przemysłowym doktoranci będą wychodzić poza środowisko akademickie i rozwijać umiejętności w przemyśle i biznesie poprzez wspólne nadzorowanie przez organizacje akademickie i nieakademickie, które mogą mieć siedzibę w tym samym państwie członkowskim UE lub państwie stowarzyszonym w ramach programu „Horyzont Europa”. Wspólne doktoraty Wspólne doktoraty stanowią wysoce zintegrowany rodzaj międzynarodowej, międzysektorowej i wielodyscyplinarnej współpracy w zakresie kształcenia doktorantów. Doprowadzają one do uzyskania wspólnych, podwójnych lub wielokrotnych tytułów doktora [2] uznawanych w co najmniej jednym państwie członkowskim UE lub państwie stowarzyszonym w ramach programu „Horyzont Europa”. Rada Nadzorcza Każda sieć doktorska MSCA powinna posiadać jasno określoną radę nadzorczą koordynującą szkolenia, badania naukowe, a w szczególności działania nadzorcze obejmujące całą sieć, zgodnie z wytycznymi dotyczącymi nadzoru nad MSCA, przy jednoczesnym ustanowieniu stałej komunikacji i wymiany najlepszych praktyk między organizacjami uczestniczącymi w celu maksymalizacji korzyści płynących z partnerstwa. Działania szkoleniowe Sieci doktoranckie MSCA powinny wykorzystywać komplementarność między organizacjami uczestniczącymi oraz sprzyjać dzieleniu się wiedzą i działaniom w zakresie tworzenia sieci kontaktów, na przykład poprzez organizację warsztatów i konferencji. Proponowane działania szkoleniowe powinny odpowiadać dobrze określonym potrzebom w różnych obszarach badań i innowacji, z odpowiednimi odniesieniami do dziedzin interdyscyplinarnych i multidyscyplinarnych, oraz być zgodne z zasadami UE dotyczącymi innowacyjnego szkolenia doktorantów [3]. Powinny one koncentrować się przede wszystkim na rozwijaniu nowej wiedzy naukowej poprzez oryginalne badania nad zindywidualizowanymi projektami. W stosownych przypadkach, gdy jest to wykonalne i korzystne dla naukowców oraz zgodne z celami projektu, zachęca się do międzysektorowego delegowania naukowców do innych organizacji uczestniczących, w tym do państw trzecich. Zwiększy to szanse na zatrudnienie naukowców spoza środowiska akademickiego. Sieci doktoranckie powinny opracowywać istotne moduły szkoleniowe dotyczące kluczowych uniwersalnych umiejętności i kompetencji wspólnych dla wszystkich dziedzin, w tym cyfrowych (np. generatywna sztuczna inteligencja), oraz wspierać kulturę otwartej nauki, waloryzację wiedzy [4] oraz, w stosownych przypadkach, innowacje i przedsiębiorczość, a także dobre postępowanie naukowe, takie jak rzetelność badawcza. W szczególności sieci doktorantów powinny odpowiednio przygotowywać doktorantów do kontynuowania kariery naukowej oraz do zwiększonej współpracy badawczej i wymiany informacji możliwej dzięki nowym technologiom (cyfrowym) (np. narzędziom współpracy, otwarciu dostępu do publikacji i innych wyników badań, w tym danych, zarządzaniu danymi FAIR, zaangażowaniu społecznemu i nauce obywatelskiej itp.). Nadzór Szczególną uwagę zwraca się na jakość ustaleń dotyczących nadzoru i mentoringu, a także poradnictwa zawodowego. Wspólny nadzór nad naukowcami jest obowiązkowy dla doktorów przemysłowych i wspólnych. Plan rozwoju kariery Plan rozwoju kariery musi zostać opracowany wspólnie przez przełożonego i każdego rekrutowanego kandydata na doktora. W przypadku wspólnego nadzoru taki plan powinien zostać opracowany z udziałem wszystkich organów nadzoru. Oprócz celów badawczych plan ten obejmuje potrzeby szkoleniowe i zawodowe naukowca, w tym szkolenie w zakresie umiejętności uniwersalnych, nauczanie, planowanie publikacji oraz udział w konferencjach i wydarzeniach mających na celu otwarcie nauki i badań naukowych dla obywateli. Plan, ustanowiony na początku rekrutacji, powinien zostać zmieniony (i w razie potrzeby zaktualizowany) w ciągu 18 miesięcy. [1] https://euraxess.ec.europa.eu/ [2] Za każdym razem, gdy niniejsza część programu prac odnosi się do stopni doktora, oznacza to, że stopnie te muszą zostać uznane za takie przez właściwe organy danego kraju lub krajów. [3] zasady_for_innowacyjny_doctoral_training.pdf [4] „Waloryzacja wiedzy” to proces tworzenia wartości społecznej i gospodarczej z wiedzy poprzez łączenie różnych obszarów i sektorów oraz przekształcanie danych, know-how i wyników badań w zrównoważone produkty, usługi, rozwiązania i polityki oparte na wiedzy, które przynoszą korzyści społeczeństwu” ( EUR-Lex - 32022H2415 - EN - EUR-Lex ). Więcej wskazówek na temat konkretnych obszarów waloryzacji wiedzy można znaleźć w kodeksach postępowania Komisji Europejskiej dotyczących zarządzania aktywami intelektualnymi, normalizacji, współtworzenia przez przemysł i środowisko akademickie oraz zaangażowania obywateli na rzecz waloryzacji wiedzy.

Sieci doktoranckie MSCA są rzeczywiście otwarte na udział organizacji z państw trzecich w celu wspierania strategicznych partnerstw międzynarodowych na rzecz szkolenia i wymiany naukowców. Te programy doktoranckie będą odpowiadać dobrze określonym potrzebom w różnych obszarach badań i innowacji, narażać naukowców na sektor akademicki i pozaakademicki oraz oferować szkolenia w zakresie badań naukowych, a także zbywalne umiejętności i kompetencje istotne dla innowacji i długoterminowych szans na zatrudnienie (np. przedsiębiorczość, komercjalizacja wyników, prawa własności intelektualnej, komunikacja). Propozycje dotyczące sieci doktorskich mogą odzwierciedlać istniejące lub planowane partnerstwa badawcze między organizacjami uczestniczącymi. Procedura naboru doktorantów musi być otwarta, przejrzysta i oparta na osiągnięciach, zgodnie z Europejską kartą naukowca. Ogłoszenie o naborze (które ma być szeroko ogłaszane na całym świecie, w tym na stronie internetowej EURAXESS [1]) musi zawierać informację, czy publikowane stawki obejmują wszystkie podatki i składki pracodawcy i pracownika. W miarę możliwości należy opublikować wynagrodzenie brutto (wynagrodzenie netto + podatki i składki pracownika). Sieci doktoranckie MSCA zachęca się do prowadzenia doktoratów przemysłowych lub wspólnych. doktoraty przemysłowe Dzięki doktoratom przemysłowym doktoranci będą wychodzić poza środowisko akademickie i rozwijać umiejętności w przemyśle i biznesie poprzez wspólne nadzorowanie przez organizacje akademickie i nieakademickie, które mogą mieć siedzibę w tym samym państwie członkowskim UE lub państwie stowarzyszonym w ramach programu „Horyzont Europa”. Wspólne doktoraty Wspólne doktoraty stanowią wysoce zintegrowany rodzaj międzynarodowej, międzysektorowej i wielodyscyplinarnej współpracy w zakresie kształcenia doktorantów. Doprowadzają one do uzyskania wspólnych, podwójnych lub wielokrotnych tytułów doktora [2] uznawanych w co najmniej jednym państwie członkowskim UE lub państwie stowarzyszonym w ramach programu „Horyzont Europa”. Rada Nadzorcza Każda sieć doktorska MSCA powinna posiadać jasno określoną radę nadzorczą koordynującą szkolenia, badania naukowe, a w szczególności działania nadzorcze obejmujące całą sieć, zgodnie z wytycznymi dotyczącymi nadzoru nad MSCA, przy jednoczesnym ustanowieniu stałej komunikacji i wymiany najlepszych praktyk między organizacjami uczestniczącymi w celu maksymalizacji korzyści płynących z partnerstwa. Działania szkoleniowe Sieci doktoranckie MSCA powinny wykorzystywać komplementarność między organizacjami uczestniczącymi oraz sprzyjać dzieleniu się wiedzą i działaniom w zakresie tworzenia sieci kontaktów, na przykład poprzez organizację warsztatów i konferencji. Proponowane działania szkoleniowe powinny odpowiadać dobrze określonym potrzebom w różnych obszarach badań i innowacji, z odpowiednimi odniesieniami do dziedzin interdyscyplinarnych i multidyscyplinarnych, oraz być zgodne z zasadami UE dotyczącymi innowacyjnego szkolenia doktorantów [3]. Powinny one koncentrować się przede wszystkim na rozwijaniu nowej wiedzy naukowej poprzez oryginalne badania nad zindywidualizowanymi projektami. W stosownych przypadkach, gdy jest to wykonalne i korzystne dla naukowców oraz zgodne z celami projektu, zachęca się do międzysektorowego delegowania naukowców do innych organizacji uczestniczących, w tym do państw trzecich. Zwiększy to szanse na zatrudnienie naukowców spoza środowiska akademickiego. Sieci doktoranckie powinny opracowywać istotne moduły szkoleniowe dotyczące kluczowych uniwersalnych umiejętności i kompetencji wspólnych dla wszystkich dziedzin, w tym cyfrowych (np. generatywna sztuczna inteligencja), oraz wspierać kulturę otwartej nauki, waloryzację wiedzy [4] oraz, w stosownych przypadkach, innowacje i przedsiębiorczość, a także dobre postępowanie naukowe, takie jak rzetelność badawcza. W szczególności sieci doktorantów powinny odpowiednio przygotowywać doktorantów do kontynuowania kariery naukowej oraz do zwiększonej współpracy badawczej i wymiany informacji możliwej dzięki nowym technologiom (cyfrowym) (np. narzędziom współpracy, otwarciu dostępu do publikacji i innych wyników badań, w tym danych, zarządzaniu danymi FAIR, zaangażowaniu społecznemu i nauce obywatelskiej itp.). Nadzór Szczególną uwagę zwraca się na jakość ustaleń dotyczących nadzoru i mentoringu, a także poradnictwa zawodowego. Wspólny nadzór nad naukowcami jest obowiązkowy dla doktorów przemysłowych i wspólnych. Plan rozwoju kariery Plan rozwoju kariery musi zostać opracowany wspólnie przez przełożonego i każdego rekrutowanego kandydata na doktora. W przypadku wspólnego nadzoru taki plan powinien zostać opracowany z udziałem wszystkich organów nadzoru. Oprócz celów badawczych plan ten obejmuje potrzeby szkoleniowe i zawodowe naukowca, w tym szkolenie w zakresie umiejętności uniwersalnych, nauczanie, planowanie publikacji oraz udział w konferencjach i wydarzeniach mających na celu otwarcie nauki i badań naukowych dla obywateli. Plan, ustanowiony na początku rekrutacji, powinien zostać zmieniony (i w razie potrzeby zaktualizowany) w ciągu 18 miesięcy. International award for research in Germany
    

    
    
        The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation is expanding its sponsorship opportunities within the Global Minds Initiative Germany funded by the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR). The Foundation’s new Humboldt Research Professorships programme initiative creates new latitudes to recruit outstanding academics to work on internationally highly competitive research topics in Germany and structurally expand fields of research.  
The new Humboldt Research Professorships allow top-tier researchers from other countries to conduct their innovative and creative research activities in Germany and establish them at German universities and research institutions without having to relinquish their posts abroad. Receiving institutions will be given flexible options for integrating and institutionally embedding the award winners, for example in the form of shared professorships or lab-to-lab professorships. Award winners are expected to initiate long-term collaborations with specialist colleagues in Germany, set up and manage an international working group in Germany and develop additional promising and creative research formats to optimally suit their research interests and methodologies. 
Humboldt Research Professors will be permitted to simultaneously continue conducting their own professorships or working groups in their countries of origin during the sponsorship. At the same time, they will also have the option to relocate fully to Germany if they choose. Long-term prospects for remaining in the country can be negotiated locally on an individual basis.

Projects should be characterized by algorithmic innovation accompanied by rigorous analysis. Of interest is research on algorithms for problems that are central to computer science and engineering, as well as new techniques for the rigorous analysis of algorithms and computational complexity. AF supports theoretical research that bounds the intrinsic difficulty of problems to determine measures of complexity in formal models of computation, classical or new. The goal is to understand the fundamental limits of resource-bounded computation and to obtain efficient algorithms operating within those limits. Research on resources other than the traditional time and space measures, such as communication and energy, is also encouraged, as is research on tradeoffs between resource use and solution quality, such as running time vs. approximation error. Rigorous analysis of properties of algorithms relating to fairness, ethics, accountability, transparency, and privacy is also in scope. In addition to the traditional sequential-computing paradigm, AF supports research on the design and analysis of novel algorithms in parallel and distributed models, as well as computational models and algorithms that capture essential aspects of computing over massive data sets. New techniques for the design and analysis of algorithms and analysis of problem complexity in areas such as optimization, cryptography, computational geometry, game theory and economics, social networks, machine learning, and numeric, symbolic, and algebraic computing are within the scope of this program. The program also supports research in algorithms needed in applied areas of research, including algorithmic research on problems arising in other areas of research on computing. While relevance to application areas is important and collaboration with researchers in these areas is encouraged, research funded by this program must advance the theoretical study of algorithms. When accompanying rigorous analysis of computational resource requirements and/or algorithmic performance measures, implementation efforts and empirical evaluation are considered strong broader impacts. Letters of collaboration from applied researchers are encouraged. Emerging topics such as quantum computing and biological models of computation are now addressed in the Foundations of Emerging Technologies (FET) program. However, projects in these areas focused on foundational issues of algorithms and complexity in these topics, as described above, can also be considered by the AF program. The Communications and Information Foundations (CIF) program supports research activities that address the theoretical underpinnings for information acquisition, transmission, and processing in communications and information processing systems. CIF projects have contributed to the development of the inter-related areas of communications, information theory, coding theory, and signal and image processing, areas that are expected to play key roles in future technology. The CIF program also supports foundational research in networked systems, such as network information theory and cross-layer design in wireless systems. Examples include secure communication, sensor networks, and other scenarios that feature massive data aggregation from distributed sensing. In addition to the traditional topics that have fueled the information revolution, there is continued interest within the CIF program in new paradigms. These include but are not limited to statistical learning and inference, signal processing on graphs and networks, multi-terminal communication problems, information-theoretic security, geometric methods in signal processing and machine learning, computational imaging, and communication-theoretic challenges associated with emerging communication technology. In the machine learning area in particular, CIF seeks to encourage research promoting paradigms based on foundational principles, rooted in information theory and statistical inference, that advance the explainability and generalizability of machine learning. Topics of interest include, but are not limited to, scalability, performance guarantees, and fundamental limits, alongside fairness and robustness of machine learning techniques. At its core, CIF is interested in the mathematical exploration of novel problem formulations rooted in the aforementioned application domains. Funding Opportunities New advanced fuel technology could lead to enhanced performance and safety of country’s reactor fleet Office of Nuclear Energy WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Nuclear Energy today announced a new funding opportunity to accelerate the research and development of silicon carbide cladding. Capable of withstanding extreme conditions within a nuclear reactor, silicon carbide is emerging as a promising advanced fuel cladding material capable of enhancing nuclear reactor safety while reducing operational costs. “The United States is home to the largest light-water reactor fleet in the world,” said Deputy Assistant Secretary of Nuclear Fuel Cycle Josh Jarrell. “Through this new funding opportunity, we’re excited to continue to work with industry on projects that can improve reactor performance and further enhance the safety of our country’s nuclear power plants, as well as inform the development of fuels to improve operational flexibility and reduce costs for future reactors.” The nation’s current reactor fleet is fueled by uranium processed into small ceramic pellets and stacked into metal tubes called fuel cladding, which are sealed at both ends to form fuel rods. Fuel cladding is a barrier between the reactor coolant and nuclear fuel pellets and is essential to protecting the fuel while also ensuring the safety of a nuclear power plant. Up to $50 million in competitive funding is available over three years to support work that will result in the fabrication of 12-foot silicon carbide cladding fuel rods for irradiation testing in research reactors. This is an important next step in the maturation of the fuel technology and will lead to the irradiation performance data required for U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission licensing and commercial deployment of the new cladding material. Interested parties can access the complete funding opportunity on Grants.gov. Applications are due by December 7, 2026. ### Committed to Restoring America’s Energy Dominance. Follow Us

LOGIN These 20 human beings are inventing new ways to harness the ever-accelerating cognitive power of agentic AI. 09-17-2026TECH The Quantum Genesis Q Competition aims to turn quantum machines from lab experiments into practical research tools. [Photo: Angel Garcia/Bloomberg via Getty Images] BY Steven Melendez The U.S. Department of Energy is launching a $215 million competition to build quantum computers that are usable in scientific research. Officials are hopeful that early versions of such machines could be operational as soon as 2028. While ordinary computers famously store data as binary digits that can take on a value of either zero or one, quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to store quantum bits, or qubits, that can take on more complex states. That means they can theoretically solve complex problems involving cryptography, the simulation of intricate biological and engineering processes, financial modeling, and potentially artificial intelligence and machine learning orders of magnitude faster than classical computers. But so far, the devices have been more the subject of scientific experimentation than useful tools in their own right. They’re generally difficult to build and sensitive to outside interference, often requiring components to be kept at temperatures close to absolute zero to avoid altering qubit data. The DOE’s Quantum Genesis Q Competition challenges applicants to deliver what the department calls “the world’s first fault-tolerant scientifically relevant quantum computers,” or SRQCs. In essence, the Energy Department is seeking to transform quantum computers from lab experiments into lab equipment, while ensuring the U.S. remains at the forefront of their development and application. The department is inviting private sector businesses to propose computers with at least 100 logical qubits capable of performing hundreds of millions of fault-tolerant operations, an achievement officials say builds on decades of research into quantum technology and computing at large. “I see it as no different than getting achievements where we could build the first particle accelerators, or incredibly new, capable telescopes,” says Darío Gil, the DOE’s undersecretary for science. “It’s a scientific instrument of the first kind—one that deals with one of the most fundamental building blocks of nature, which is quantum mechanics.” Fast Company & Inc © 2026 Mansueto Ventures, LLC Fastcompany.com adheres to NewsGuard’s nine standards of credibility and transparency. In the simplest terms, the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) seeks to determine whether it’s possible to build an industrially-useful computer by 2033. Specifically, QBI is designed to rigorously verify and validate whether any quantum computing approach can achieve utility-scale operation — meaning its computational value exceeds its cost.
QBI is not a competition between performers: DARPA is interested in evaluating all viable approaches for which there is available funding. Successful performers will progress through three stages:
In addition to funding performers, QBI will add value to their ongoing research and development efforts by providing unbiased third-party verification and validation of an organization’s path to a utility-scale quantum computer. QBI will also effectively communicate the results of this verification and validation effort to other U.S. government stakeholders.
QBI is an expansion of the existing DARPA Underexplored Systems for Utility-Scale Quantum Computing (US2QC). QBI is separate from but related to the existing Quantum Benchmarking (QB) program, which sought to determine the yardstick for impact.

descricao_completa: BASS Growth Projects are a new funding framework designed to help space-enabled solutions that have already achieved demonstrable commercial success in a primary market to unlock secondary market opportunities. The scope of Growth Projects includes the development, integration and testing of new service elements to meet the requirements of secondary markets, as well as the implementation of large-scale pilots. ESA BASS Growth Projects are aimed at ambitious companies or industrial teams which have developed a space-enabled solution that has already been validated in the primary market. This funding opportunity is intended as a springboard for business growth by supporting expansion into new markets. Optional Support: Some companies applying for Growth Projects may not yet have a fully established ecosystem to commercialise their solution at scale and may need to expand their network of partners. For this reason, the Growth Project framework offers optional support to assist companies with establishing strategic partnerships, expanding the value chain, enabling access to global markets and managing the business risks associated with the identified market opportunities. This will be done by connecting applicants with strategic players from the Growth Projects Partner Network. This network, established by ESA, brings together business multipliers, investors, accelerators, consultancies, users, customers, and data or asset providers, with the objective of fostering strategic partnerships that strengthen the value chain, facilitate access to global markets, and mitigate business risks by connecting projects with organisations able to provide relevant expertise, resources, or market access. If your company can provide some of the support described above, scroll further down for more information. The optional support includes access to: Please see the detailed co-funding rules below: Please note that funding participation is open to groups, organisations and businesses that reside in ESA member states that have subscribed to BASS. Currently these countries are Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. To start the application process you will first need to create an account on ESA's Open Space Innovation Platform (OSIP). The application process follows a standard three-step process: Growth Project Questionnaire (GPQ) > Outline Proposal > Full Proposal Within the GPQ form, the company can indicate areas of support required at the point of submission. Once the GPQ step has successfully passed to the next stage, ESA will support when possible by, for example, facilitating introductions with members of the Growth Projects Partner Network. Please note that a Written Authorisation for ESA Funding must be submitted together with the Full Proposal – applicants are advised to contact their National Delegation(s) as early as possible in the process to obtain one. Apply for a Growth Project We are inviting expressions of interest from investors, accelerators, consultancies, business multipliers, and organisations interested in collaborating, testing, or adopting emerging space-enabled services. By joining this network, you will gain access to future matchmaking opportunities designed to connect relevant partners and support collaboration across the space-enabled ecosystem. Investors: It is a high-level objective for ESA to foster commercialisation of and private investment in the European Space industry. As part of this network, investors have early visibility and access to Growth Project candidates. Accelerators, Consultancies and Business Multipliers: Accelerators, consultancies and business multipliers are invited to participate in future exchanges and matchmaking events to support Growth Project candidates establish strategic partnerships, expand their value chain, enable access to global markets and manage the business risks. Organisations interested in supporting Growth Projects as users or customers: ESA will be supporting Growth Project candidates with matchmaking to users and customers whenever this is required. descricao_resumida: The tendering process follows a structured, sequential approach, with each successive stage building on the content and feedback of the preceding stage. You are advised to inform your National Delegation(s) of your intention to submit a proposal as soon as possible, as you will need to have their written authorisation for ESA funding to proceed at the Full Proposal stage. To help you with the application process, we have a network of Ambassadors available to provide you with high-quality business consultancy support. If your activity originates from a Kick-start, Proof-of-Concept or Enabling Study, ESA may recommend that you can go straight to Step Three – but you will still require authorisation from your National Delegation(s).
descricao_completa: The tendering process follows a structured, sequential approach, with each successive stage building on the content and feedback of the preceding stage. You are advised to inform your National Delegation(s) of your intention to submit a proposal as soon as possible, as you will need to have their written authorisation for ESA funding to proceed at the Full Proposal stage. To help you with the application process, we have a network of Ambassadors available to provide you with high-quality business consultancy support. If your activity originates from a Kick-start, Proof-of-Concept or Enabling Study, ESA may recommend that you can go straight to Step Three – but you will still require authorisation from your National Delegation(s). If you are in this position, please obtain confirmation from your ESA contact person about whether this is applicable to you. The first step is to tell us concisely about your preliminary concept by submitting the Activity Pitch Questionnaire (APQ). ESA can then provide you with feedback and – if your APQ is accepted – guide you on the next steps. Once your APQ has been accepted, the next step is to submit an Outline Proposal. This must be done within two months of your APQ submission. Your Outline Proposal will be evaluated by ESA, with feedback and approval provided as appropriate in due course. Upon acceptance of the Outline Proposal, you will be invited to prepare a Full Proposal, incorporating ESA’s feedback. You must do this within four months of your Outline Proposal being approved. Written Authorisation of ESA Funding (AOF) from the relevant National Delegation(s) covering the full scope of the proposal must accompany the Full Proposal when it is submitted for evaluation via esa-star . The Full Proposal will be evaluated by a Tender Evaluation Board (TEB). In case of a positive proposal evaluation, the TEB recommends the activity for implementation, pending answers to any clarification points identified. Once negotiations are successfully completed, the project kick-off will be agreed, and the agreement will be sent for signature. descricao_completa: Sendo um sistema estruturante e tendo o Sistema de Gestão de Parcerias da União (Sigpar) como estruturador, conforme o Decreto nº 11.271/2022, o Transferegov.br é a solução tecnológica em si e representa a evolução da antiga Plataforma +Brasil. A alteração do nome atendeu aos requisitos do padrão Gov.br, bem como deixar mais intuitiva a relação entre a marca e o tema Transferências. Com dados abertos, o Transferegov.br operacionaliza de forma informatizada as transferências de recursos oriundos do Orçamento Fiscal e da Seguridade Social da União. Entre os principais objetivos da Transferegov.br, estão a padronização, a simplificação e a rastreabilidade dos processos de transferências de recursos da União, comportando cada uma das modalidades dessas transferências com suas características particulares e instrumentalizando sua gestão pelos entes envolvidos na busca da efetividade nas entregas de políticas públicas para a sociedade. Cumpre observar que, inicialmente, a Transferegov.br operacionaliza os instrumentos descritos no art. 3º do Decreto nº 10.035, de 2019. Todavia, é objetivo do governo federal internalizar na referida Plataforma todas as modalidades de transferências de recursos da União, tornando mais eficiente e transparente a gestão desses recursos, tanto para o Estado brasileiro quanto para fins de controle pela própria sociedade. Já o parágrafo único do referido artigo, assegura a possibilidade de que as transferências executadas por instrumentos não previstos no caput do art. 3º também sejam operacionalizadas no Transferegov.br, sob condição da celebração de Acordo de Cooperação Técnica - ACT entre o Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos e o órgão ou a entidade responsável pelas respectivas transferências. No plano de trabalho do referido ACT, deve constar como uma das etapas a ser realizada e o Mapeamento do processo da Transferência a ser internalizada. descricao_completa: Um prédio em Florianópolis que deu origem a uma incubadora de empresas. Um fundo de fomento à ciência e tecnologia que se transformou em uma fundação de apoio à ciência e tecnologia – e que, mais tarde, incorporou a inovação em seu nome e em seu DNA. Essa é uma pequena síntese da história da Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa e Inovação do Estado de Santa Catarina (Fapesc), que completou 26 anos em 9 de janeiro de 2023. Para chegar até aqui a Fapesc percorreu um longo caminho. Seu embrião é o Fundo Rotativo de Fomento à Pesquisa Científica e Tecnológica do Estado de Santa Catarina (Funcitec), criado em 1990 logo após a aprovação da Constituição de Santa Catarina e uma grande mobilização no Estado em prol da CTI. Na época, também constituiu-se o Tecnópolis, um espaço planejado para receber empresas de tecnologia em Florianópolis, atual ParqTec Alfa. Neste período foi realizado um convênio com a Fundação Certi, ligada à Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina (UFSC), que originou o Celta, uma incubadora com espaço físico de 10.500 metros quadrados, que iniciou com 27 empresas incubadas – a sede da Fapesc fica neste prédio. É deste período também a criação da Rede Catarinense de Ciência e Tecnologia (RCT), que levaria internet ao ecossistema de CTI do Estado. Em 1997 houve mais um passo nesta jornada. O fundo foi extinto e deu origem à Fundação de Ciência e Tecnologia, que manteve a sigla Funcitec. Em 2008, foi criada a Lei Catarinense de Inovação,que definiu a Fapesc como “agência de fomento executora da política estadual de ciência, tecnologia e inovação”. Um ano depois foi elaborada a Política Catarinense de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação. A Lei Complementar nº 534, de 2011, definiu o nome da instituição: Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa e Inovação do Estado de Santa Catarina, incorporando a inovação no nome e consolidando-a entre os programas fomentados pela Fapesc. Em 2020, a identidade visual foi alterada, com o objetivo de trazer a inovação para a forma como a fundação se apresenta, valorizando o conhecimento e as pessoas. Criação do Fundo Rotativo de Fomento à Pesquisa Científica e Tecnológica (Funcitec) Extinção do Fundo e criação da Fundação Funcitec. Atualmente Fapesc. Alteração do nome Funcitec para Fapesc. ao nome e atribuição da Fapesc Aprovado o atual estatuto da Fapesc. Reformulação da estrutura administrativa da Fapesc. Realização do planejamento estratégico. Atualização da Missão. Ampliação dos programas de fomento e chamadas públicas. Início da Jornada dos 25 anos. Ampliação dos recursos para CTI. Comemoração de 25 anos da Fapesc. Comemoração dos 26 anos da Fapesc. Impulsionar o ecossistema catarinense de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação por meio do fomento, da integração institucional e do apoio à pesquisa e à inovação, promovendo o desenvolvimento sustentável, o equilíbrio regional e a melhoria da qualidade de vida da sociedade catarinense. Ser referência nacional e internacional na atuação pública estratégica e no fortalecimento do ecossistema de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação, reconhecida pela excelência, integridade e impacto no desenvolvimento de Santa Catarina.
